commit_message:
Optimize SET/INCR*/DECR*/SETRANGE/APPEND by reducing duplicate computation (#13505)

- Avoid addReplyLongLong (which converts back to string) the value we
already have as a robj, by using addReplyProto + addReply
- Avoid doing dbFind Twice for the same dictEntry on
INCR*/DECR*/SETRANGE/APPEND commands.
- Avoid multiple sdslen calls with the same input on setrangeCommand and
appendCommand
- Introduce setKeyWithDictEntry, which is like setKey(), but accepts an
optional dictEntry input: Avoids the second dictFind in SET command

---------

Co-authored-by: debing.sun <debing.sun@redis.com>

fix_commit.message: avoid possible use-after-free with module KSN changes (#13875)
fix_commit.author: Oran Agra

findings.title: Use-after-free in incrDecrCommand: reply built from robj after keyspace notification can free it
findings.message: incrDecrCommand() was changed (in PR #13505) to reply to the client with addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new) -- reading the string value directly from the 'new' robj that now represents the key's value -- instead of replying with the integer value that had been copied onto the stack (addReplyLongLong(c, value)). This reply call was placed AFTER signalModifiedKey() and notifyKeyspaceEvent() are invoked. notifyKeyspaceEvent() can synchronously invoke registered keyspace-notification module hooks, and such a hook may call RM_StringDMA (or otherwise mutate/replace the string) on the very key that was just incremented/decremented. Since 'new' may no longer be a shared integer object (the optimization added a fast-path reusing the object only under narrow conditions; otherwise it's a freshly allocated, refcount==1 string object owned by the dict), a module hook that frees or reallocates the underlying sds buffer leaves 'new' as a dangling pointer. The subsequent addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new) then reads freed/stale memory -- a use-after-free. This previously went unnoticed because for small values Redis used shared integer objects, so dropping/replacing a reference didn't actually free the object; the refactor's use of a real heap-allocated string object for the reply source, combined with calling the reply function after the notification hook can run, exposed the UAF.
findings.suggestion: Build/queue the client reply using the value BEFORE invoking signalModifiedKey()/notifyKeyspaceEvent(), so no module hook can mutate or free the underlying object between computing the reply source and actually sending the reply. The upstream fix moves addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new) to immediately after the object is stored in the keyspace (before signalModifiedKey/notifyKeyspaceEvent/server.dirty++).

ground_truth.root_cause: PR #13505 optimized INCR/DECR (and related commands) to avoid re-serializing the integer to a string for the reply, by replying directly from the heap-allocated robj ('new') that was just stored into the keyspace, rather than from a stack-local integer copy. However the reply-generation call was left positioned after signalModifiedKey()/notifyKeyspaceEvent(), which can re-enter into module keyspace-notification subscriber callbacks. Those callbacks run with full API access (including RM_StringDMA) to the key that now holds 'new', so they can free/reallocate the buffer 'new' points to before the deferred reply call reads it. Previously, replies used a stack copy of the integer value (or values were small/shared integer objects that aren't actually freed by dict replacement), so no live reference into freed heap memory was retained across the notification call.
